descriptionChirho: Qal (and Nifal) intransitive sense of being satisfied, full, or having plenty, encompassing all person/number/gender inflections including perfect, imperfect, imperative, consecutive, cohortative, infinitive construct, infinitive absolute, and participle forms across the full paradigm.

Qal sense with negative connotation meaning to be sated to excess, to have too much of something, to be disgusted or wearied, as shown by Korean 싫증내다 ('be sick of'), Spanish 'harto' ('fed up'), Swahili 'kuchoka' ('to tire of'), and Hindi अघाना ('be surfeited').

Hifil and Piel causative sense meaning to satisfy or fill someone, to give enough to eat, encompassing all causative inflections including perfect, imperfect, imperative, consecutive, infinitive, and participle forms with various pronominal suffixes.
